method: Implements the bencode grammar from BitTorrent BEP 3. Decoding reads the whole input as UTF-8 bytes and accepts exactly one value: i<digits>e integers, <length>:<bytes> byte strings, l…e lists and d…e dictionaries. Integers may be negative but must not use leading zeros or negative zero, and must stay within the safe integer range of ±9,007,199,254,740,991. Byte-string lengths are decimal byte counts with no leading zeros and must fit inside the input. Dictionary keys must be byte strings in strictly increasing bytewise order, so unsorted and duplicate keys are refused. Truncation, trailing data, nesting deeper than 64 levels and inputs longer than 200,000 characters are refused, and every structural error reports the byte offset. Encoding parses the supplied JSON with JSON.parse, sorts object keys by their UTF-8 bytes, writes strings as UTF-8 byte strings, arrays as lists and whole numbers as integers, and refuses decimals, booleans, null and unsafe integers because bencode has no such types. Decoded byte strings are shown as UTF-8 text with JSON escaping, or as uppercase 0x-prefixed hex when the bytes are not valid UTF-8; a dictionary key is shown the same way and keys that would collide after display are refused. No encryption, hashing of piece data, file writing, account access or network request is performed.
